Une charge financière qui pèse lourdement sur les économies concernées, souligne l'économiste nigériane Iyabo Masha, directrice du Groupe des 24. « La dette freine la croissance, parce que les pays ne disposent plus de ressources suffisantes pour financer leur développement, ou parce qu'ils consacrent l'essentiel de leurs ressources au remboursement de leurs dettes », précise-t-elle.

The designation, contained in the US State Department's 2026 Trafficking in Persons (TIP) Report, means Nigeria could face restrictions on specific security assistance and commercial licences for military equipment from 1 October, unless the restrictions are waived or an applicable exception is granted by US President Donald Trump. Keep up with the latest headlines on WhatsApp | LinkedIn Nigeria is among 14 countries included on the 2026 Child Soldiers Prevention Act (CSPA) list, alongside Afghanistan, Burma, the Central African Republic, the Democratic Republic of the Congo, Ethiopia, Iran, Russia, Rwanda, Somalia, South Sudan, Sudan, Venezuela and Yemen. Under Section 402 of the CSPA, the US government identifies foreign governments whose armed forces, police, other security forces or government-supported armed groups allegedly recruit or use child soldiers.

stories.title: DRC Ebola outbreak passes 9,000 cases, including more than 4,000 deaths
stories.summary: The worst Ebola outbreak ever in the Democratic Republic of Congo has passed the 9,000-case mark, with the number of deaths exceeding 4,000 since early October, health authorities said Tuesday.

stories.title: Nigeria: Military Plane Crash - Traditional Ruler Cries Out As Decaying Bodies 'Pollute' Community's Source of Drinking Water
stories.summary: Nigeria: Military Plane Crash - Traditional Ruler Cries Out As Decaying Bodies 'Pollute' Community's Source of Drinking Water Premium Times Nigeria plane crash sparks fears of drinking water contamination. 13 October 2026 Premium Times (Abuja) By Oluwole Josiah "This same river where the plane crashed into is what supplies our drinking water. We have a water treatment machine at Aboto about seven kilometres away from here. The water doesn't come every day, and when it comes, it is this same water that flows there, pumped to be treated for our drinking. So, it means whatever happens, pollution is already in the river, either as a result of decayed bodies or as oil that dropped into the river." A humanitarian crisis may hit Igbokoda, the headquarters of Ilaje Local Government Area of Ondo State, following the pollution of the source of water for the community by decaying bodies of the victims of the Nigeria Air Force (NAF) plane that crashed there last week. The traditional ruler of the community, Afolabi Odidiomo, told PREMIUM TIMES on Tuesday that the body of water has been polluted, leaving the people with contaminated water both for drinking and other domestic uses.

stories.title: Nigeria: Tinubu Transmits Bills On Genocide, War Crimes Prosecution to House of Reps
stories.summary: Nigeria: Tinubu Transmits Bills On Genocide, War Crimes Prosecution to House of Reps Asiwaju Bola Ahmed Tinubu Bola Ahmed Tinubu 13 October 2026 Premium Times (Abuja) By Sharon Eboesomi The bills seek to repeal the existing Geneva Conventions Act, establish provisions for punishing genocide, war crimes and crimes against humanity, and strengthen Nigeria's cooperation with the International Criminal Court. President Bola Tinubu has transmitted two bills to the House of Representatives seeking to strengthen Nigeria's legal framework for prosecuting genocide, war crimes and crimes against humanity. The bills, which were forwarded to the House for consideration, seek to domesticate key international legal instruments and establish provisions for punishing serious international crimes under Nigerian law. The president's letter, dated 6 October and addressed to the Speaker of the House, Abbas Tajudeen, was read during plenary on Tuesday. Follow us on WhatsApp | LinkedIn for the latest headlines Titled "Transmission of the Geneva Conventions and Additional Protocols Bill, 2026 and the Rome Statute of the International Criminal Court (Enforcement) Bill, 2026 for consideration", the letter invoked Section 58(2) of the 1999 Constitution, as amended. "Pursuant to Section 58(2) of the Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria, 1999 (as amended), I forward herewith the Geneva Conventions and Additional Protocols Bill, 2026 and the Rome Statute of the International Criminal Court (Enforcement) Bill, 2026 for the kind consideration of the House of Representatives," Mr Tinubu said.

stories.title: Kenya: Court of Appeal Clears Kenya-U.S. Health Deal for Implementation Pending Appeal
stories.summary: Kenya: Court of Appeal Clears Kenya-U.S. Health Deal for Implementation Pending Appeal Kriddl / Wikimedia Commons (CC0) Kenya's Supreme Court (file photo). 13 October 2026 Capital FM (Nairobi) Nairobi — The Court of Appeal has cleared the way for the implementation of Kenya's health cooperation framework with the United States, overturning High Court orders that had blocked the programme over constitutional concerns. A three-judge bench set aside conservatory orders issued on December 19, 2025, ruling that the public interest in maintaining essential healthcare services outweighed the risks associated with allowing the programme to proceed while the legal dispute remains unresolved. The judges warned that continued suspension of the framework could disrupt critical healthcare services, including treatment for HIV, tuberculosis (TB), malaria and other infectious diseases, as well as immunisation programmes. Keep up with the latest headlines on WhatsApp | LinkedIn "The lives of citizens who depend on treatment for HIV, TB, and malaria, provided under the Framework risk being negatively and irredeemably impacted," the judges ruled. "Some even risk losing their lives which is an irreversible consequence," they added.

stories.title: Kenya: Laikipia Confirms Two Suspected Ebola Cases Test Negative
stories.summary: Kenya: Laikipia Confirms Two Suspected Ebola Cases Test Negative John James/ UNICEF A tent used to isolate Ebola patients is disinfected in Bunia, DR Congo. 13 October 2026 Capital FM (Nairobi) Nairobi — Laikipia County health authorities have confirmed that two suspected Ebola virus disease cases tested negative, urging residents to remain calm and avoid spreading unverified information following an outbreak of concern in Nanyuki. The clarification comes after reports of a suspected Ebola case at Nanyuki Teaching and Referral Hospital triggered anxiety among residents on Monday. Speaking to the media on Tuesday, Laikipia County Executive Committee Member for Health Albert Taiti said the county had activated precautionary measures after a patient presented with symptoms resembling those of Ebola virus disease. Taiti said health officials collected samples from the patient and sent them for laboratory testing, with the results confirming that the patient did not have Ebola. Follow us on WhatsApp | LinkedIn for the latest headlines However, he disclosed that the patient died while receiving treatment at the facility.

stories.title: Kenya: Ruto Says Opposition Has No Plan for Kenya, Pledges Development Ahead of 2027 Polls

stories.title: Malawi: Malawi Urged to Build Economic Resilience As World Economy Wobbles
stories.summary: Malawi Urged to Build Economic Resilience As World Economy Wobbles VOA Malawi on map. 14 October 2026 Nyasa Times (Leeds) Malawi cannot afford to rely on external demand or donor support as the global economy slows, according to a senior Reserve Bank of Malawi economist, who has warned that the country is underperforming even by regional standards and must accelerate reforms to strengthen economic resilience. Analysing the implications of the latest World Economic Outlook projections, economist Kisu Simwaka said the expected moderation in global growth to 3.1 per cent from 3.5 per cent signals a more challenging external environment for African economies, particularly those dependent on commodity exports and foreign aid. "The message is clear: the world economy is slowing down. And Malawi must accelerate," Simwaka said. Keep up with the latest headlines on WhatsApp | LinkedIn He argued that weaker global growth, coupled with sluggish expansion in Europe, was already being reflected in Malawi's export performance. Tobacco earnings, the country's largest foreign exchange earner, reached US$287.1 million by early October 2026, down sharply from US$526.2 million during the same period a year earlier.

stories.title: Malawi: Bushiri Extradition Order Thrown Out As Malawi Court Delivers Final Ruling
stories.summary: Malawi: Bushiri Extradition Order Thrown Out As Malawi Court Delivers Final Ruling Prophet Shepherd Bushiri Prophet Shepherd Bushiri 14 October 2026 Nyasa Times (Leeds) Prophet Shepherd Bushiri and his wife Mary have won a major legal victory after the High Court in Lilongwe delivered its final ruling crushing efforts to extradite them to South Africa. In a detailed 175-page judgment, the court laid out the reasons behind its earlier decision to throw out an extradition order issued against the couple, dealing a significant blow to South Africa's long-running bid to bring them back to face legal proceedings. The latest ruling confirms the court's position that the extradition order granted in March 2025 could not stand because of serious procedural and legal flaws. Among the most damaging findings was that the Bushiris were denied their right to be heard before the extradition order was made, a development the court found was sufficient to invalidate the process. Keep up with the latest headlines on WhatsApp | LinkedIn The decision cements the couple's courtroom triumph and effectively slams the brakes on attempts to send them back to South Africa under the now-quashed order.

stories.title: RDC: des archives météo révèlent que le bassin du Congo se réchauffait déjà dans les années 1960
stories.summary: RDC: des archives météo révèlent que le bassin du Congo se réchauffait déjà dans les années 1960 Le bassin du Congo se réchauffait déjà fortement dans les années 1960. C'est ce que révèle une étude publiée lundi 12 octobre 2026 dans la revue scientifique Earth System Dynamics . Une étude qui s'appuie sur un jeu de données météorologiques inédit : des notes manuscrites, parfois vieilles de plus de 60 ans, retrouvées et numérisées, qui viennent combler une lacune dans les connaissances sur l'histoire climatique de la région. Publié le : 14/10/2026 - 07:00 1 min Temps de lecture Des milliers de relevés météorologiques datant de plusieurs décennies sont conservés dans les archives de l’Institut national pour l’étude et la recherche agronomiques (INERA), à Yangambi, en République démocratique du Congo (RDC). Ces documents permettent aux scientifiques de retracer l’évolution du climat dans la région.

stories.title: South Africa: Two ANCYL Members Shot Dead in Ekurhuleni, Three Others Wounded
stories.summary: South Africa: Two ANCYL Members Shot Dead in Ekurhuleni, Three Others Wounded SAPoliceService/X South African police tape. 14 October 2026 Daily Maverick (Johannesburg) By Felix Dlangamandla A shooting at a memorial service in Ekurhuleni on Tuesday has left two ANC Youth League members dead and three others injured. Two ANC Youth League members, aged 21 and 23, were shot dead in Katlehong, Ekurhuleni, on Tuesday evening, 13 October 2026, when a gunman, after firing shots in the air, turned his rifle on a crowd of mourners. Three others were injured and rushed to hospital. The injured, according to police spokesperson Brigadier Brenda Muridili, are aged between 12 and 27. After the shooting, the suspect handed himself in and is in police custody, Muridili said.

stories.title: Africa: 'Need for UN Has Never Been Greater,' UN Chief Says, Proposing Slimmer $3.3 Billion Budget for 2027
stories.summary: Africa: 'Need for UN Has Never Been Greater,' UN Chief Says, Proposing Slimmer $3.3 Billion Budget for 2027 Aotearoa/Wikimedia Commons United Nations member country flags at the UN Headquarters in New York (file photo). 13 October 2026 UN News Service Amid climate disruption, an AI revolution, war and growing hunger, "the need for the United Nations has never been greater," Secretary-General António Guterres said on Tuesday, presenting a $3.3 billion programme budget proposal for next year - a cut of $40.8 million. Key points The proposed 2027 programme budget is 1.2 per cent below the 2026 approved level UN80 Initiative reforms will continue, with more cuts, staff relocations and the abolition or downgrading of some posts Predictable cashflow and timely payment of dues are essential as efficiency gains will not be sufficient to resolve the liquidity crisis Divisions deepening Follow us on WhatsApp | LinkedIn for the latest headlines "The challenges before us are profound ," Mr. Guterres told the General Assembly's Fifth Committee, comprising all 193 UN Member States that handle administrative and budgetary matters at UN Headquarters in New York. "Geopolitical divisions continue to deepen, conflicts persist across regions and humanitarian needs are soaring, international law is trampled, climate disruption is hitting every continent and artificial intelligence is reshaping economies and societies," said the Secretary-General. Moreover, the planet's collective Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), aimed at leaving no one behind, "are slipping further from reach" , Mr. Guterres said. "And yet, in this era of uncertainty and fragmentation, the need for the United Nations has never been greater," he declared.

stories.title: South Sudan: As South Sudan Plans for Elections, a Town Counts the Cost of War
stories.summary: South Sudan: As South Sudan Plans for Elections, a Town Counts the Cost of War Hedley Tah/WFP Loading finished, the cargo plane is ready for take-off - bound for South Sudan's conflict-hit Jonglei State. 13 October 2026 The New Humanitarian (Geneva) By Patricia Huon Akobo, South Sudan — "We've never had capable leaders who could translate people's struggle into meaningful action." A looted school with scattered benches and children attending lessons beneath a tree. A maternity ward, where a woman had collapsed outside and given birth in the grass. A food distribution site, where hundreds of people were waiting beneath the sun. Keep up with the latest headlines on WhatsApp | LinkedIn Since renewed fighting between government and opposition forces erupted across large parts of South Sudan last year, collapsing the country's fragile peace agreement, Akobo, in the east, has been one of the flashpoints. Now, thousands who fled the fighting are coming home, exposing the scale of the challenges facing the town and reflecting the wider humanitarian emergency impacting the country, which is supposed to be preparing for its first ever elections. "People's livelihoods have been destroyed," said Mac Anyang Yuang, a team coordinator in Akobo for the UN's World Food Programme (WFP). "They depend entirely on food assistance." The South Sudanese government, led by President Salva Kiir from the ruling SPLM party, formed a unity administration with the opposition SPLM/A-IO in 2020.

stories.title: Cameroun: le président Paul Biya fixe les priorités du budget 2027, sans préciser le calendrier électoral
stories.summary: Cameroun: le président Paul Biya fixe les priorités du budget 2027, sans préciser le calendrier électoral Au Cameroun, Paul Biya fixe le cap du prochain budget de l'État, mais laisse planer le doute sur le calendrier électoral. stories.title: Tchad-France: une «déclaration d’intention» signée pour relancer la coopération militaire

stories.title: Nigeria: la méga-raffinerie Dangote prolonge son entrée en Bourse pour attirer les investisseurs africains

stories.title: Africa: Rice Is a Strategic Commodity for Economic Transformation Says African Development Bank Group
stories.summary: Rice Is a Strategic Commodity for Economic Transformation Says African Development Bank Group 13 October 2026 Content from a Premium Partner African Development Bank (Abidjan) announcement The African Development Bank Group has brought its financing plans and investment initiatives to the centre of discussions at a West Africa Rice Investment Roundtable, held in Accra, Ghana. The roundtable was held June 2-3 and brought together governments, investors, development institutions, and private sector leaders to explore ways to turn the Economic Community of West African States Regional Rice Roadmap into a more impactful reality. Opening the Roundtable on behalf of the President of the Republic of Ghana, Professor Naana Jane Opoku-Agyemang, Vice President of the Republic of Ghana said: "West Africa has the land, water, knowledge, and entrepreneurial spirit required to feed itself...Investing in rice means investing in jobs, industries, rural prosperity, and economic resilience. The time has come for Africa to produce what it consumes and consume what it produces." Richard Ofori-Mante, the Bank Group's Director of Agricultural Finance and Rural Development, who attended the event said achieving rice self-sufficiency in West Africa will require sustained investment from seed systems and irrigation to processing, storage, logistics, and market access. "Rice is not merely a crop; it is a strategic commodity for economic transformation. Reducing import dependence and strengthening regional value chains will improve food security, create employment opportunities, strengthen rural economies, and retain wealth within the region," Ofori-Mante said.

stories.title: Zimbabwean author denies using AI to write award-winning story
stories.summary: Image source, Caine Prize / Seth Avusuglo Image caption, Simbarashe Kundizeza says he was inspired by a poem about fish tanks to write a story about his family struggles in Zimbabwe By Lucy Fleming Published 14 October 2026, 00:31 BST Zimbabwean writer Simbarashe Kundizeza has denied using artificial intelligence (AI) to write his short story, which won this year's Caine Prize for African Writing. stories.title: Les Pléiades, magnifique amas d’étoiles observable à l'oeil nu,  dans le ciel d'Afrique
stories.summary: Ciel d'Afrique Les Pléiades, magnifique amas d’étoiles observable à l'oeil nu, dans le ciel d'Afrique Publié le : 13/10/2026 - 17:10 Il y aura de belles choses à observer dans le ciel africain au cours des prochaines semaines. Le soir, dans les prochains jours, la planète Mercure sera difficilement visible très basse sur l’horizon ouest, juste après le coucher du Soleil, mais il faudra avoir un horizon bien dégagé si vous souhaitez relever le challenge. Les Pléiades © Luc Viatour Publicité Saturne, la planète aux anneaux, sera beaucoup plus facile à repérer : elle brillera toute la nuit dans la constellation du Verseau, avec la Lune à proximité les 23 et 24 octobre.Pour observer Jupiter et Mars, il faudra plutôt veiller : les deux planètes seront visibles en seconde partie de nuit, entre les constellations du Lion et du Cancer. Enfin, début novembre, Vénus fera son retour dans le ciel du matin, à l’horizon est. Ovidiu Bujorean, chief executive officer of OviBees Ventures, spoke with Wasim Tahir, Senior Advisor at ODI Global and Research Fellow at the Harvard Center for International Development, for the third conversation of Wave 2 of the RootsToFoods Capital Series. stories.title: Lockerbie bombing suspect seized from Libya in 'cloak and dagger' operation
stories.summary: Figure caption, Media outlet Libyan Review broadcast footage of Abu Agila Mas'ud Kheir Al-Marimi in a US prison By David Cowan Scotland home affairs correspondent Published 12 October 2026 Updated 13 October 2026 A Lockerbie bombing suspect has claimed he was illegally removed from Libya to stand trial in the United States after "a cloak and dagger operation conducted in the dead of night". Abu Agila Mohammad Mas'ud Kheir Al-Marimi has alleged he was abducted by armed men and handed over "hooded and bound" to FBI agents, who had a plane waiting to fly him out of the country. Al-Marimi, also known as Mas'ud, has denied building and priming the bomb that brought down Pan Am Flight 103 over Lockerbie on 21 December 1988, killing 270 people. The Libyan argues he was the victim of an unlawful rendition and has asked a judge in Washington DC to throw the case out of court. In response, the US Department of Justice said, under American law, the manner of his removal should not stop his thrice-postponed trial from finally getting underway in January.

During an event held last October for people to pay their respects to Odinga, three people were shot dead after mourners attempted to gain access to the VIP section of Nairobi's Kasarani Stadium by force. The 40-year-old - who was only diagnosed with the deadly infectious disease after arriving seriously ill at a Nairobi hospital - became Kenya's first confirmed case. He died two days later on 5 October. That his infection went undetected at multiple health facilities in the Democratic Republic of Congo and two airport health screenings in Uganda and Kenya has raised serious questions about these nations' biosecurity during a significant outbreak. More than 4,000 people have died from Ebola in DR Congo this year, in what is the second most deadly known outbreak to date.

Ali is the British-Somali boxer who escaped to the UK from the Somali civil war with her family as a refugee, and in 2021 became the first person to box for Somalia at Olympic Games . The boxing significance of her last name is actually not mentioned in the film – and I never noticed it until it flashed up in a kind of “fight card” intertitle before her first competitive bout. She is fiercely played by Jasmine Jobson, from TV’s Top Boy; her supportive white Muslim-convert husband Richard – a hugely important figure in enabling Ramla to break away from her disapproving family and do as she wants – is played by Finn Cole, and her abusive trainer Clinton is Gershwyn Eustache Jr. This is a film that takes you through the classic boxing-movie scenes fluently enough: the nervous first appearance in the gym, the overbearing quasi-parental coach, the heartstopping fight debut.

stories.title: ICJ judge Navi Pillay wins Nobel peace prize for promoting international law
stories.summary: 1:11 Nobel peace prize winner Navi Pillay jokes about sharing award with Donald Trump – video ICJ judge Navi Pillay wins Nobel peace prize for promoting international law Committee recognises work of South African who chaired UN commission that concluded Israel was guilty of genocide in Gaza The Nobel peace prize has been awarded to Navi Pillay, the South African former UN human rights chief who chaired the UN commission that concluded Israel was guilty of genocide in Gaza . The Norwegian Nobel committee said Pillay, who is serving as a judge at the international court of justice (ICJ), has “shown that legal measures can help prevent acts of war and violence”. “Navi Pillay’s commitment to universal legal principles and her firm moral compass are constants in a long career,” the committee said, mentioning her early work defending Nelson Mandela under South Africa’s apartheid regime, serving on the international criminal tribunal, and then as the UN high commissioner for human rights, as well as chairing the UN independent international commission of inquiry on the occupied Palestinian territory. That commission concluded last year that the state of Israel was guilty of genocidal acts in Gaza “with the specific intent to destroy Palestinians in Gaza”, and said the country’s prime minister, Benjamin Netanyahu, its president, Isaac Herzog, and its former defence minister Yoav Gallant had “incited the commission of genocide”. “It is clear that there is an intent to destroy the Palestinians in Gaza through acts that meet the criteria set forth in the genocide convention,” Pillay said on the publication of the commission’s findings in September last year. Israel refused to cooperate with the commission, arguing it was biased, and rejected its report as “scandalous”. The Israeli foreign ministry reacted furiously to news of Pillay’s award on Friday. “If there were an award for lies, hatred, and blood libels, Navi Pillay wouldn’t just be a contender.

stories.title: Why Zimbabwe tycoon 'Sir Wicknell' was loved and hated in Africa
stories.summary: Image source, Zanu-PF Image caption, Wicknell Chivayo, who had a fleet of personalised luxury cars, loved white Rolls-Royces By Ish Mafundikwa Reporting from Harare Published 8 October 2026 Wicknell Chivayo, the Zimbabwean tycoon who died in a helicopter crash along with his wife Lucy Muteke last week, divided opinion in life and continues to do so in death. He called himself "Sir Wicknell", a nod to the embellishment that epitomised his lifestyle - and a nickname some used for the 45-year-old who packed enough controversy into his short life to last several lifetimes. He was relentlessly self-documenting, building much of his public persona on social media, where he posed with piles of cash and announced the cars and money he gave to people whom he considered deserving. Chivayo delighted in displaying his access to heads of state across Africa and showing off his possessions, conducting video tours of his fleet of expensive cars, mainly Rolls-Royces, with vanity plates, watches and a vast collection of designer shoes. His admirers saw a fabulously wealthy man sharing his good fortune.
